title: kv-cache: improved eviction heuristics for fragmentation, paging and GPU spillover
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and naive LRU-based eviction frequently cause suboptimal memory utilization and excessive GPU-to-host spillover under mixed-sequence workloads. This PR implements a multi-factor eviction policy that combines allocation-aware defragmentation hints, page-granularity paging, and spillover priority tiers to reduce costly GPU memory churn and tail latency. Design: 1) Track allocation fragment metadata per allocation bucket to prefer evicting small, hot-sparse fragments that free contiguous pages for future large KV items. 2) Introduce a lightweight paged backing store for oversized spillover entries that splits very long key-value segments into page frames to avoid single huge spill ops. 3) Add a spillover priority tier system: cold-prefetch, warm-evictable, and hot-protected; the scheduler uses request age and token-frequency heuristics to assign tiers. 4) Integrate eviction decisions with the continuous-batching forecaster so batches avoid thrashing pages on known upcoming prefixes. Implementation notes: new data structures live behind a feature-flag (kv_spill_v6) and default-off for clusters with older drivers. Core changes are in runtime/kv_cache/* and runtime/scheduler/* with small API additions to the runtime metrics layer to export fragmentation_ratio, page_faults, and spill_latency_breakdown. Benchmarks: on internal perf-lab workload mix (chatty short context + long-context retrieval), end-to-end median tail P95 token latency reduced by ~12% on A100 with 80GB KV working set and measured GPU spill I/O reduced by ~28%. Memory usage fragmentation_ratio dropped from ~0.32 to ~0.12. Safety and rollout: feature-flag rollout, gradual ramp to Dedicated regions with canary policy, and runtime telemetry added for automated kill-switch if spill_latency increases >2x. Tests: unit tests for pager correctness, integration tests with continuous-batching simulator, and a stress test in perf-canary harness. Checklist: Ensure Linear tickets closed, add release notes, monitor perf dashboards post-merge.
commits_summary: initial: add paging backing store and allocation metadata
refactor: move eviction decision path into ordered priority tiers
perf: reduce lock contention in defragmentation path
tests: add pager unit tests and continuous-batching integration tests
docs: flag docs and rollout notes
review_comments: Diego: Can you quantify the worst-case CPU overhead of the paging layer? Asha: Worst-case single-threaded pager overhead is ~4% in our synthetic test, but amortized under batching it's <1%.
Linh: The defrag path still takes the global allocator lock briefly; consider handoff to cooperative background thread. Author: added a cooperative defrag pass and moved heavy work off hot path.
Marcus: Add an opt-out env for Dedicated customers that need deterministic eviction behavior. Author: added cluster-level config and admin toggle.
QA: stress test showed a rare race with fragment metadata on reorder; fixed by adding atomic version check and new unit test.
ci_checks: e2e-canary: passed on canary-2 after rerun
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory utilization and reduces GPU spillover and tail latencies by introducing page-granular spillback, fragmentation-aware eviction, and spillover priority tiers. Feature-flagged rollout; monitoring and kill-switch added.
